articles.title: Intrinsic backward emission of coherent Raman photons from homogeneous media
articles.authors: Jitendra Nath Acharyya, G. Benni, A. Sentenac, H. Rigneault, Sandro Heuke
articles.summary: In four-wave mixing the driving wavevectors set the output direction, so coherent Raman light can be sent backwards without any structure in the sample. The authors show that coherent Stokes Raman scattering (CSRS) phase-matches efficiently into the backward collection cone of a high-NA objective, and identify an azimuthally polarized Stokes annulus with a circularly polarized pump as the best geometry. With a ~790 nm pump and 1,030 nm Stokes, backward CSRS near 1,470 nm was detected on an InGaAs APD, giving about 7×10⁹ backward photons/s from sunflower oil. They imaged avocado, human fatty liver, sheep brain myelin and PMMA edges at ~330 nm lateral and 0.92 µm axial resolution. Backward flux is ~20× below forward CARS, narrowing to ~5× after detector efficiency.
articles.why: A refocusable coherent Raman signal that does not rely on sample scattering opens same-side detection for thick tissue, opaque substrates and fibre-based probes.

articles.title: Microfluidic Brillouin platform for frequency-resolved mechanics of complex fluids
articles.authors: Chingis Kharmyssov, Vsevolod Cheburkanov, Mykyta Kizilov, Brian Sanders, Evren Oktem, Ankit Kumar, Abhishek Jain, Vladislav V. Yakovlev
articles.summary: We introduce an integrated microfluidic platform that combines pressure-flow rheology with depth-resolved Brillouin microspectroscopy to investigate complex fluids in extensive frequency ranges. Apparent viscosity is measured via calibrated pressure-flow in a rectangular polydimethylsiloxane microchannel, while GHz-frequency Brillouin spectroscopy probes longitudinal mechanics under identical steady-flow conditions. Using semi-dilute methylcellulose solutions in a cell-culture medium as a model, we reveal mild shear-thinning behavior, whereas the Brillouin frequency shift and linewidth values remain constant throughout the flow rate range, mainly influenced by polymer concentration. …
articles.why: Couples pressure-flow rheology with depth-resolved Brillouin microspectroscopy on one microfluidic chip, linking low-frequency viscosity and GHz longitudinal mechanics under identical flow.

articles.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 µm
articles.authors: Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi
articles.summary: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 µm is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 µm has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. …
articles.why: Quantum infrared spectroscopy measures IR absorption with only visible/near-IR lasers and detectors; extending it to 20 µm opens the long-wave region that photon-pair sources had not reached.

CNN1 performed binary tumor/non-tumor prediction and CNN2 histotype classification. CNN1 was evaluated against blinded neuropathologist SRH consensus and CNN2 against the final integrated histopathological diagnosis. …
articles.why: Bicentric clinical study of fiber-laser SRH with CNNs on recurrent brain tumors, where therapy-induced changes make frozen sections hard to read; validated against blinded neuropathologists.

articles.title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D-IR Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Kölbel J, Sévery L, Fernández-Terán RJ
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives
articles.summary: Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi-step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two-dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main-group hydrides. …
articles.why: A direct spectroscopic route to X–H bond dissociation free energies in solution, replacing radical-equilibration and multi-step thermodynamic cycles; useful for PCET and HAT chemistry.

articles.authors: Ersland EE, Mehrotra DR, Brisebois H, Han L, Grinstaff M, Schaer T, Bergholt MS, Snyder BD, Albro M
articles.summary: Raman spectroscopy captures the molecular fingerprints of living tissues without labels or tissue destruction. Translating these spectra into absolute measures of tissue biochemical composition remains a challenge owing to tissue-dependent optical properties, variations in sampling volume, and lack of normalization standards requisite for quantitative scaling. Here we introduce a scheme to derive the biochemical constituents of a tissue expressed as a percentage of the tissue wet weight, like biochemical assays, from Raman spectra measured optically. …
articles.why: Converts tissue Raman spectra into absolute composition (percent of wet weight, like a biochemical assay), addressing the normalization problem that keeps Raman semi-quantitative.

articles.title: A-scan Raman microspectroscopy based on remote focusing with a planar mirror
articles.authors: Jisheng Zhang, Junjiang Liu, Pengfei Lai, Fuzhou Shen, Guanjingyun Wang, Xiangguo Yuan, Linyuan Zhao, Xingyun Wang, Huihong Wu, Daohong Xie, Ling-juan Zhang, Wenjie Liu, Quan Liu

articles.summary: Conventional depth-resolved Raman microspectroscopy relies on point-by-point axial scanning, which is slow and increases the risk of photodamage. To address this issue, we have developed A-scan Raman microspectroscopy, named after A-scan in ultrasound imaging, which is based on remote focusing with a planar mirror that maps the axial information of a sample into the lateral dimension for snapshot depth-resolved Raman measurements. Raman spectra from 21 distinct depth positions are captured simultaneously in a single snapshot. …
articles.why: Borrows the ultrasound A-scan idea: remote focusing maps depth onto the camera, giving Raman spectra from 21 depths in one snapshot instead of slow point-by-point axial scanning.

As a result, current wide-field implementations are typically restricted to fields of view (FOVs) below 200 μm and to either the fingerprint or high-wavenumber spectral regions. …
articles.why: Pushes wide-field mid-infrared photothermal imaging past the usual sub-200 µm field of view to millimetre scale, with a picosecond OPO tunable across both fingerprint and high-wavenumber regions.

articles.title: Frequency-swept Brillouin spectroscopy
articles.authors: Lin Kang, Shahrin Jahan Jaima, Jitao Zhang
articles.summary: Spontaneous Brillouin microscopy provides non-contact access to the viscoelastic properties of materials. Standard measurements typically utilize a single-wavelength continuous-wave laser to illuminate a specimen and excites a spontaneous Brillouin scattering signal, which is then recorded by a spectrometer. Existing Brillouin spectrometers are mostly built around either a scanning Fabry-Pérot etalon or a virtually imaged phased array (VIPA) etalon. While performing well, these setups are bulky and demand significant optical expertise to construct and maintain. Here, we propose a new approach to conducting Brillouin spectroscopy. …
articles.why: Replaces the bulky scanning Fabry–Pérot or VIPA spectrometer with a frequency-swept scheme, which could make Brillouin microscopy simpler to build and maintain.

articles.title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
articles.authors: Zhibin Hu, Tianrun Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Pengcheng Fu, Ziyang Huang, Bo Chen, Bangjie Song, Minglu Li, Xinyu Deng, Quan Zhou, Delong Zhang, Siying Peng
articles.summary: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. …
articles.why: Resonant metasurfaces amplify the photothermal signal while keeping fast thermal recovery, so weak vibrational changes at the cell membrane can be imaged in living cells during an enzymatic lipid conversion.

institutions: Southern University of Science and Technology

Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide-a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. …
articles.why: Rotational-anisotropy Raman finds broken phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO₂, giving optical evidence in the debate over whether it is an altermagnet.

Here, we introduce TERS-ABNet, a deep-learning framework that reformulates single-molecule structure determination as an image-to-graph inference task. …
articles.why: Turns tip-enhanced Raman maps into complete single-molecule structures with deep learning (image-to-graph inference), reducing reliance on expert interpretation of ambiguous TERS signatures.

The first approach uses discrete wavenumber images using two key bands at 1546 and 2922 cm -1 to screen leukocytes. …
articles.why: A label-free differential white-cell count from ordinary blood smears using single-cell optical photothermal IR spectra, without stains or flow cytometry.

articles.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
articles.authors: Masato Fukushima, Keiichiro Toda, Yusei Sugawara, Shotaro Kawano, Takuro Ideguchi
articles.summary: Volumetric mid-infrared photothermal (MIP) imaging has been limited by a trade-off between speed and signal-to-noise. Pairing a high-power nanosecond mid-IR source with rapid angular scanning in optical diffraction tomography, the authors reach 19.2 volumes per second, roughly 400 times faster than earlier MIP tomography, with SNR above 70 and no temporal averaging. They track lipid droplets in 3D inside living cells and find heterogeneous, anomalous diffusion from full volumetric trajectories. Sweeping the mid-IR wavenumber gives hyperspectral volumes over a 300 cm⁻¹ window in about one second.
articles.why: About 400× faster than earlier mid-infrared photothermal tomography: 19 chemical volumes per second without averaging, enough to follow lipid droplets moving in 3D inside living cells.

articles.summary: This study investigates the effect of repeated mechanical recycling on the thermal and chemical properties of polypropylene (PP). Virgin PP (v-PP) was subjected to three recycling cycles (r1-PP, r2-PP, r3-PP) through repeated melting. Thermal degradation behavior was analyzed using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), while chemical structural changes were examined using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). TGA result showed a single step degradation for all samples. …

articles.title: UV-Induced Degradation Behaviour of HDPE, PET and NBR Films: An FTIR Analysis
articles.authors: Zuhayra Mohd Zulfikar
articles.journal: Enhanced Knowledge in Sciences and Technology
articles.summary: his study investigates the ultraviolet (UV) degradation behaviour of high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) under controlled UV irradiation at 254 nm. Chemical changes induced by photo-oxidation were analysed using Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. The formation of oxygen-containing functional groups, particularly carbonyl and hydroxyl groups, was used as an indicator of degradation. Results showed that HDPE exhibited early- stage oxidation and increased brittleness, while NBR underwent moderate degradation involving both chain scission and crosslinking. …

articles.authors: Mohammad Umair Farooqui, Ubed Ur Rehman Mughal, Salman Ahmed, Kanwal Hussain, Bilawal Shaikh, Arslan Ahmer, Arfa Azhar, Saleem Ahmed Joyo, Shayan Ahmed, Rabeia
articles.summary: Objective: To prepare dexlansoprazole–Soluplus® solid dispersions by solvent evaporation, compare their saturation solubility at pH 1.2 and pH 6.8 and evaluate drug–polymer compatibility using Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Methods: Dexlansoprazole–Soluplus® dispersions were prepared at drug-to-polymer ratios of 1:1,1:2 and 1:3 using 95% ethanol. The solvent was removed by rotary evaporation, followed by vacuum drying, pulverization and sieving. Physical appearance, practical yield and drug content were evaluated. Saturation solubility was determined by the shake-flask method at pH 1.2 and pH 6.8 at 37 ± 0.5°C for 48 hours, with spectrophotometric quantification at 285 nm. …

articles.summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of the Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) model in Islamic Religious Education learning through ablution practice which includes planning, implementation, and evaluation of learning. The problem of this research is that Islamic Religious Education learning is still oriented towards theoretical delivery of material so that student engagement and understanding are not optimal, especially in practical material. This study uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive type which was implemented at Ma'arif Seputih Raman Junior High School, Central Lampung Regency. …
